title: The Romans invade Britain
fact: AD 43: the Roman army of Emperor Claudius invades. The Romans stay for about 400 years.

title: Hadrian's Wall is built
fact: AD 122: Emperor Hadrian orders a wall across the north of England to keep out the Picts. Parts of it still stand.

title: The Romans leave Britain
fact: AD 410: the Roman army leaves to defend other parts of the Empire, and never comes back.

title: The Vikings first raid Britain
fact: AD 789: Vikings from Denmark and Norway first raid Britain. Many later settle in the east and north of England.

title: The Battle of Hastings
fact: 1066: William of Normandy beats Harold at the Battle of Hastings and becomes king.

title: The Domesday Book
fact: 1086: William the Conqueror has every town and village in England surveyed. The record is the Domesday Book.

title: Magna Carta
fact: 1215: King John is forced to agree to Magna Carta, which limits the king's power.

title: Wales is joined to England
fact: 1284: Edward I's Statute of Rhuddlan joins Wales to the English Crown. He builds huge castles such as Conwy and Caernarfon.

title: The Battle of Bannockburn
fact: 1314: Robert the Bruce beats the English at Bannockburn.

title: The Black Death
fact: 1348: the Black Death arrives and kills about a third of England's population.

title: The Battle of Agincourt
fact: 1415: Henry V beats the French at Agincourt.

title: The Wars of the Roses begin
fact: 1455: civil war between the House of Lancaster (red rose) and the House of York (white rose).

title: The Battle of Bosworth Field
fact: 1485: Henry VII wins at Bosworth Field. The Wars of the Roses end and the Tudors begin.

title: The Spanish Armada is defeated
fact: 1588: the English navy defeats the Spanish Armada, under Elizabeth I.

title: James VI of Scotland becomes James I of England
fact: 1603: James VI of Scotland also becomes James I of England. One king for both countries.

title: The Gunpowder Plot
fact: 1605: Guy Fawkes and other Catholics try to blow up Parliament and King James I. Remembered on 5 November.

title: The Civil War begins
fact: 1642: civil war between the king's Cavaliers and Parliament's Roundheads.

title: Charles I is executed
fact: 1649: Charles I is executed and England becomes a republic.

title: The Restoration
fact: 1660: the monarchy is restored and Charles II becomes king.

title: The Great Fire of London
fact: 1666: the Great Fire destroys much of London. Wren rebuilds St Paul's. (600 years after Hastings.)

title: The Glorious Revolution
fact: 1688: William of Orange replaces the Catholic James II.

title: The Act of Union with Scotland
fact: 1707: the Act of Union joins England and Scotland as the Kingdom of Great Britain.

title: The Battle of Culloden
fact: 1746: Bonnie Prince Charlie loses at Culloden, the last battle fought on British soil.

title: The Act of Union with Ireland
fact: 1801: Ireland joins, making the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland.

title: The Battle of Trafalgar
fact: 1805: Nelson beats the French and Spanish fleets at Trafalgar and is killed.

title: The slave trade is abolished
fact: 1807: the slave trade is abolished. Slavery itself ends in the Empire in 1833.

title: The Battle of Waterloo
fact: 1815: Wellington beats Napoleon at Waterloo. (600 years after Magna Carta.)

title: The Reform Act
fact: 1832: the Reform Act gives more men the vote and abolishes 'rotten boroughs'.

title: The Irish famine begins
fact: 1845: the potato crop fails in Ireland. About a million people die and many more emigrate, many to Britain and America.

title: The Great Exhibition
fact: 1851: the Great Exhibition is held in the Crystal Palace in Hyde Park.

title: The Crimean War begins
fact: 1853: Britain and its allies go to war with Russia in the Crimea. Florence Nightingale nurses the wounded.

title: Married women can keep their own earnings
fact: 1870: an Act of Parliament lets married women keep their own earnings. Before this they belonged to the husband.

title: The First World War begins
fact: 1914: the First World War begins. It ends on 11 November 1918.

title: Women over 30 get the vote
fact: 1918: women over 30 get the vote for the first time.

title: Ireland splits in two
fact: 1922: the south of Ireland becomes the Irish Free State. Northern Ireland stays in the UK.

title: Women vote at 21, the same as men
fact: 1928: women can vote at 21, on the same terms as men.

title: The Second World War begins
fact: 1939: Britain declares war after Germany invades Poland. The war ends in 1945.

title: The NHS is founded
fact: 1948: the National Health Service is founded. (600 years after the Black Death.)

title: The voting age drops to 18
fact: 1969: the voting age is lowered from 21 to 18.

title: The UK joins the EEC
fact: 1973: the UK joins the European Economic Community.

title: The Good Friday Agreement
fact: 1998: the Good Friday Agreement brings peace to Northern Ireland.

title: The Scottish Parliament and Welsh Assembly open
fact: 1999: the Scottish Parliament and the Welsh Assembly open.

title: The London Olympics
fact: 2012: London hosts the Olympic Games for the third time, after 1908 and 1948.
